newsitem.title: USA: Lobbyist indicted in probe of ex-ag. secretary.
newsitem.headline: Lobbyist indicted in probe of ex-ag. secretary.

text.p: A federal grand jury has indicted lobbyist Richard Douglas on charges of giving illegal gratuities to former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy and masterminding illegal political donations to Espy's brother, it was announced Wednesday.

The 19-count indictment also accused Douglas of "material false statements" to federal investigators and with wire fraud in obtaining a mortgage. Douglas worked for Sun-Diamond Growers of California, the nation's largest fruit cooperative, at the time of the alleged offenses.

Sun-Diamond was convicted last month of violating federal law on charges dealing with the same gifts to Espy and the donations to his brother's unsuccessful campaign for Congress. James Lake, a partner in a Washington public relations firm, pleaded guilty earlier this year to wire fraud and election law violation in the donations.
Douglas and Espy were college roommates. Espy resigned his cabinet post in 1994 amid accusations he had taken illegal gifts and favors from companies he was supposed to regulate.

In its trial, Sun-Diamond argued that the gifts, which included lavish meals, luggage and tickets to the 1993 U.S. Open tennis tournament, were due to friendship and were not an attempt to sway Espy's judgment or win favorable policies.
Espy has repeatedly denied breaking the law.
